messages:
alex.k: Hey team — customer (FinWave) wants a short POC to validate Private/VPC connectivity for a Private deployment. They need: preserve client src IP, TLS inspection in their DMZ, and fallback to a proxy if PrivateLink traffic is denied. Asking: PrivateLink vs VPC peering tradeoffs + minimal firewall rules and cost/impact.

maria.s: Quick Qs — is the POC in AWS only? and do they control egress (onprem) or will we terminate in their VPC?

alex.k: AWS only for now, they'll run the inference containers in our Private package inside their VPC. They control egress and insist on TLS inspect for traffic leaving to internet. They also want us to keep original client IP to make auth decisions.

ben.n: Notes from network side: preserving client src IP + PrivateLink = tricky. Interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) terminate to ENIs in customer subnet; traffic to our service will show source IP of the original client only if there's no SNAT in the path. If they put a NAT Gateway or proxy in front of the PrivateLink ENI, we'll see the proxy IP instead.

ben.n: If they need true client IP preservation to our containers, two options:
- Use VPC peering/transit path where packets are routed directly and we avoid SNAT (requires route table entries and cross-account peering/transit setup).
- Use PrivateLink but configure a transparent on-host proxy or preserve srcip by avoiding NAT on the path (rare).

maria.s: For POC simplicity I'd recommend PrivateLink with an explicit design that preserves source IP via cross-account ENI routing where possible. If they can't avoid TLS-inspect proxying, we should fallback to "proxy on egress" model — i.e., customer terminates TLS -> proxy -> outbound to our PrivateLink IPs; then we'll see proxy IPs.

jess.s: Pricing check — does PrivateLink change our billing? Customer asked if there's extra cost per hour or per GB we should account for.

ben.n: Customer costs: AWS charges per-ENI/hour and per-GB for data processed by interface endpoints in some regions. For us: Private deployment pricing should include extra networking egress we route through their NAT/proxy; we should add note in the SOW about potential egress bandwidth charges and PrivateLink hourly endpoint charges.

kevin.t: Security checklist — if TLS-inspection is in place, they must provide a trusted CA chain and cert pinning guidance. Also need to confirm if their TLS-inspect will reissue certs (breaks mTLS) — if yes, we need a plan for client auth.

alex.k: They also asked for firewall rules they can paste into their team. Can we draft a minimal allowlist?

ben.n: Minimal rules for PrivateLink (interface endpoint model):
FIREWALL: allow outbound TCP 443 to our interface endpoint ENI IPs (per-ENI IP list)
If using proxy: allow outbound TCP 443 to proxy IP(s) and from proxy to endpoint ENIs
If using peering: allow all traffic between the two VPC CIDR blocks on ports 443 and 10250 (k8s health if needed)

ben.n: Example ACL snippet (customer AWS SG):
```
Type: Outbound
Protocol: TCP
PortRange: 443
Destination: <our-interface-endpoint-eni-ips>  # replace with the ENI list
Description: Allow Redwood inference TLS
```

maria.s: Also ask them to provide the VPC CIDR(s), the transit VPC / TGW topology, and the proxy NAT IPs. Without that we can't give exact ENI IP list.

alex.k: They said they can share a sanitized diagram tomorrow. POC timeline: 2 weeks (setup + smoke tests). Who owns the runbook?

jess.s: I'll own commercial side + SOW language. Maria/Ben can own the network runbook. Kevin to sign off on security Qs.

kevin.t: Security deliverables for POC:
- TLS inspection behavior document (does it reissue certs?)
- List of allowed FQDNs for our control plane (for monitoring/metrics)
- KMS/HSM integration notes if they want to manage keys on-prem

maria.s: For smoke tests let's do: 1) curl to model endpoint from a test pod (check x-forwarded-for or srcIP), 2) long request stream to validate streaming + TLS proxied, 3) tokenized cost sample to estimate egress.

alex.k: Can we provide a minimal set of FQDNs/IPs they should allow outbound to our control plane?

ben.n: Yes — control plane egress (examples):
- api.redwood-inference.com (443)
- metrics.redwood-inference.com (TLS, 443)
- s3-us-east-1.amazonaws.com (if we need to pull model artifacts)
We should give them CIDR ranges for our egress proxies (will send in follow-up).

ops-bot: Deployment notice — Private control plane can be hosted in us-east-1 or customer region. Canary planned in us-east-1 on 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC.

alex.k: Next actions:
- Maria/Ben: draft network runbook + sample SG/ACL config (by EOD tomorrow)
- Kevin: list security Qs to send to customer (by EOD)
- Jess: include PrivateLink cost note in SOW draft and flag egress bandwidth caveat (by EOD)
- Alex: get sanitized VPC diagram from customer and paste here when available

maria.s: I'll include two variants in the runbook: PrivateLink-first (with proxy fallback) and Peering-first (preserve srcIP).

jess.s: Sounds good — I'll schedule the pre-POC call for Mon as well.

alex.k: Awesome, thanks.

kevin.t: :thumbsup:

ben.n: FYI — if they insist on TLS inspect + mTLS to our service, we might need to offer a dedicated private deploy on their subnet to avoid reissue issues. I'll add that as a note in the runbook.

alex.k: Great input. I'll wait for the diagram and then we can lock the POC network design.
